issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) requires a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int, but the solution implementation declares a static method with the name computeMealCost(Meal) while the solution's Main calls calculateTotalPrice. This name/signature mismatch between the solution's SealSaloon and Main (and between solution and the problem spec) is a structural inconsistency that will prevent the code from compiling or from matching the expected API described in the exercises.
issues.suggestedFix: Align method names and signatures across artifacts: implement a static method calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int in SealSaloon (as specified in the problem statement) and update any callers to use calculateTotalPrice. Alternatively, if computeMealCost is preferred, update the problem statement and all callers (e.g., Main) to refer to computeMealCost to ensure consistent API naming.

issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) names the meal-cost method calculateTotalPrice(Meal), but the code uses a different identifier computeMealCost(Meal). This mismatch appears across artifacts (problem vs. code) and even within the solution repository (Main calls calculateTotalPrice while SealSaloon defines computeMealCost). Students may be confused which method name to implement/call because the specification and code examples disagree.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose one canonical method name and apply it everywhere. Either (A) rename the method computeMealCost(Meal) to calculateTotalPrice(Meal) in SealSaloon and update all call sites (Main.java and any tests), or (B) update the problem statement and UML to refer to computeMealCost(Meal). Ensure all examples and commented code use the same identifier so students can unambiguously map the requirement to the implementation.
